> **Reading this table.** *(not resolved)* under Version means the component is **declared** in `vcpkg.json` but its feature is not enabled in this configuration, so there is no installed tree to read a version from. It is not shipped in this build; a version appears once the stage that needs it turns the feature on.

> **Attribution owed** is never empty: every licence here requires that the component copyright notice and licence text be retained and shipped (Tech-Stack-Plan.md 8.1), so the cell says what is owed rather than whether anything is. `licence text` is that baseline. **Apache-2.0 alone** adds 4(d), propagating an upstream `NOTICE` file verbatim, which is why only those rows mention NOTICE: `and NOTICE` means one was found, `NOTICE not checked` means the component is not built in this configuration so nothing was looked for, and `NOTICE MISSING` means the installed tree was there and the file was not -- a release blocker. The licence files live in `res/licenses/`, are reproduced in About -> Third-Party Notices and in the installed `licenses` folder, and are verified by the release gate (8.3). `res/licenses/` does not exist yet; populating it is Stage 15 work.

## Licence elections

Where a component is offered under more than one licence, the one we take is recorded here explicitly rather than inferred.

- **libjpeg-turbo** — libjpeg-turbo is offered under IJG / BSD-3-Clause / zlib. We ELECT IJG, matching Tech-Stack-Plan.md 6.2.
- **freetype** — FreeType is dual-licensed FTL / GPL-2.0. We ELECT FTL. FTL requires a credit in the documentation, which the Third-Party Notices dialog provides.
- **hunspell** — Hunspell is tri-licensed 'MPL-1.1 OR LGPL-2.1-or-later OR GPL-2.0-or-later' (verified against upstream license.hunspell and vcpkg's port manifest, 2026-08-18). We ELECT the LGPL branch, and because that grant is '2.1 OR LATER' we take it specifically as LGPL-3.0 -- the same licence as Qt. That means one obligation model covers both libraries: dynamic linking, user-replaceable binaries, and a corresponding-source offer. Electing MPL-1.1 would have been lighter (file-level copyleft, no relinking obligation) but would add a second, differently-shaped set of obligations to track and release-gate.
- **gcc-runtime** — libstdc++-6.dll, libgcc_s_seh-1.dll and libwinpthread-1.dll are shipped beside the executable, never statically linked. The Runtime Library Exception permits distributing a program under any licence, INCLUDING PROPRIETARY, provided it was produced by an Eligible Compilation Process -- i.e. stock GCC with no non-free plugin. TA-9 and license-audit both check that condition.
- **mingw-w64-runtime** — The mingw-w64 runtime is a permissive mix (public domain / ZPL-2.1 / MIT / BSD-2) recorded per component. Zlib is used here as the representative expression; the per-component breakdown is owed before release.
- **pdfium** — Consumed as a DLL through its FPDF_ C API (verified T12, 2026-08-18), so the compiler that built it does not matter. Read and raster only -- every write goes through our own COS layer. NOTE: the prebuilt archive ships only the packager MIT licence; PDFium own BSD-3-Clause text and its third-party notices must be fetched into res/licenses/ before release.
- **qt** — Qt is taken under LGPL-3.0, linked dynamically and shipped as replaceable DLLs. Never -static; never signature-locked or anti-tampered.

## Notes

- Qt is linked **dynamically** and shipped as replaceable DLLs beside the executable. It is never statically linked, never signature-locked, and never anti-tampered: user-replaceability is an LGPL-3.0 obligation and is release-gate tested.
- The GCC runtime (`libstdc++-6.dll`, `libgcc_s_seh-1.dll`, `libwinpthread-1.dll`) is `GPL-3.0-or-later WITH GCC-exception-3.1`. The exception is what permits shipping proprietary binaries, and it holds only while the build uses stock GCC with no non-free plugin.
- RawPage's own source is proprietary. No file in `core/`, `pdf/`, `ui/`, `app/`, or `platform/` may be copied from a copyleft project.
